summary: The new file is close, but the PR is incomplete and currently misreports some failure modes: the recall standup is not wired into the existing own-clocks dispatcher, `--standup` exits successfully on elevation refusal, and the `--once` path leaves several expected setup/ledger failures uncaught.

findings.message: This change adds `cosmos_recall_clock.standup()`, but `_call_standup()` still has no `if name == "recall"` branch. The existing own-clocks entrypoint therefore continues to return `{"ok": false, "error": "unknown standup recall"}`, so the new standup code is unreachable from the central launcher/matrix path the work order targets.

`main()` returns exit code 0 when `needs_elevation` is true, even though `standup()` has already set `ok=False` and `registered=False` for that case. Any automation that keys off process status will treat an unregistered task as successfully installed and skip the manual elevation step.

The `--once` path only handles `RecallError`. `CosmosPaths(root)`, `install_key.bin.read_bytes()`, and `Ledger(...)` can all fail with other exceptions (for example `CosmosPathError`, `FileNotFoundError`, or `LedgerError`), which will currently surface as an uncaught traceback from the scheduled task instead of a typed refusal/JSON result like the other clock entrypoints.
